subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser-specific public URL/domain/path denylist and warnlist, or fold this into a broader cross-tool egress security policy?
rationale: The request would create operator-facing security/config surface, and the related open issues show competing browser-only, private-network, and generic egress scopes that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Design browser policy first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser navigation deny/warn semantics, redirect/proxy behavior, defaults, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold into generic egress policy
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39685 the canonical direction if maintainers want one policy for browser, web_fetch, web_search, and plugin HTTP egress.

options.title: Reject browser denylist surface
options.body: Close this after documenting that current hostname exceptions and external network controls are the supported approach for bot-blocked public sites.

recommendation.title: Design browser policy first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser navigation deny/warn semantics, redirect/proxy behavior, defaults, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal across browser SSRF defaults, browser navigation behavior, and shared network policy work.
